subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: How should OpenClaw classify and act on plain `LLM error api_error: Internal server error` during cron fallback chains?
rationale: Current main intentionally separates structured `server_error`, timeout, overloaded, and shared auth-profile cooldown behavior, and the prior broad overloaded-classifier PR was closed unmerged.

options.title: Narrow cron-local server-error handling
options.body: Classify plain internal-server API failures as a cron/fallback transient, fast-fail or short-budget repeated candidates, retry/back off, and avoid poisoning shared auth-profile health by default.

options.title: Fold into broader guardrails
options.body: Move the remaining behavior into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/14376 and close this only after that item explicitly covers plain provider 500 fast-fail and notifications.

options.title: Use profile-wide overloaded cooldown
options.body: Treat the plain API 500 path as overloaded/auth-profile health, accepting the risk that one provider outage can cool down shared profile state across sessions.

recommendation.title: Narrow cron-local server-error handling
recommendation.body: Classify plain internal-server API failures as a cron/fallback transient, fast-fail or short-budget repeated candidates, retry/back off, and avoid poisoning shared auth-profile health by default.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed the merged overlapping structured server_error cron retry change and are the best visible human routing candidate for the remaining policy choice.
